$comment: Chalkdraw palette source (revision 4). src/build.js generates themes/*.json from this file.
name: Chalkdraw

git.$comment: Git status scale. Within a mode the six hued statuses share one oklch lightness and chroma and differ only in hue; 'ignored' is a deliberate neutral and sits outside the ramp.

rules.fieldColor: equals identifier in all three variants
rules.commentPolicy: comments must stay readable, not faded below the punctuation color
rules.variantPair: Deep and Flat are an exact inversion: the same two greys swapped between editor and chrome. Changing one requires mirroring the other.
rules.inkDerivation: Dark punctuation is the identifier color at 86% per channel; the line number is 44%. The build recomputes both when the identifier changes.
rules.gitScale: Git decoration colors come from the `git` group, not from ui.warning/ui.success. Within a mode the six hued statuses share one (L, C) in oklch and differ only in hue, so any adjustment moves the whole mode, never a single status. 'ignored' is exempt.
rules.coolPalette: Chalkdraw Cool sits at roughly 140% of Deep's syntax chroma, and strings (#E8C79A) are the only warm hue in the code -- identifiers are a warm-neutral chalk white, everything else is cool. If the palette is retuned, that relationship holds: raise or lower the whole set together and keep strings as the single warm note. The surfaces are lightness-matched to Flat in oklch (editor L 0.2295, panels L 0.2121) with Cool's blue hue preserved, and punctuation is lifted to the lightness Deep's 86% ink rule would give, so operators read as brightly as identifiers.
rules.coolFields: Cool is the one variant where field/property/variable (#A4BDD6) differs from the default foreground (#F2F0E8). Deep, Flat and Paper keep them equal.
